1.2.1.5.rationale: Generic NAD(P)+-dependent aldehyde dehydrogenase; distinct from the acetylating acetaldehyde dehydrogenase activity (EC 1.2.1.10) that is fused in bifunctional AdhE. No literature describes a second fused catalytic activity for this EC.
1.2.1.5.evidence: none found specific to EC 1.2.1.5; PMID 40301148 (ALDH superfamily review) reports no fusion for this activity

1.1.1.71.rationale: NADP+-dependent alcohol dehydrogenase, characterized across many organisms as a standalone enzyme. No literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

3.6.3.44.rationale: Generic ABC-type transport ATPase (ATP phosphohydrolase); searches returned no reports of a fused second catalytic activity beyond ATP hydrolysis coupled to transport.

3.6.3.1.rationale: Ca2+-transporting ATPase (P-type ion pump); standalone ion-motive ATPase activity with no reported second catalytic activity.

3.6.3.17.rationale: Carbohydrate/monosaccharide-transporting ATPase; no literature describing a fused second catalytic activity.

3.6.3.18.rationale: Transport-associated ATPase; EuropePMC search returned zero relevant hits, consistent with a narrowly characterized, monofunctional transporter ATPase.

3.6.3.23.rationale: Polyamine/other-substrate-transporting ATPase; EuropePMC search returned zero relevant hits, consistent with a monofunctional transporter ATPase.

1.14.14.1.rationale: Unspecific monooxygenase covering the broad cytochrome P450 superfamily; the vast majority require a separate partner reductase. A rare self-sufficient fusion (e.g. P450 BM3/CYP102A1, fusing heme and reductase domains) exists but is an atypical bacterial variant, not characteristic of this EC class.
1.14.14.1.evidence: none found indicating fusion is characteristic of the class; CYP102A1/P450BM3 self-sufficient fusion is a known but non-representative exception

2.4.1.241.rationale: UDP-galactose-dependent digalactosyldiacylglycerol synthase, a standalone glycosyltransferase; no literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

1.6.5.2.rationale: NADH:quinone oxidoreductase (respiratory Complex I / NDH-1); although a large multi-subunit complex, all subunits cooperate in one overall electron-transfer/proton-pumping catalytic activity rather than two distinct EC-type activities.
1.6.5.2.evidence: none found specific to this EC describing a second fused catalytic activity

2.7.1.1.rationale: Hexokinase; literature on its role in sugar/glucose signaling (e.g. plant HXK nuclear signaling) is a regulatory/moonlighting function, not a second EC-type catalytic activity, per the explicit worked example in the task instructions.
2.7.1.1.evidence: none found for a second catalytic activity; sugar-signaling literature (e.g. PMID 42796823) describes moonlighting, excluded by instructions

1.14.13.72.rationale: EC 1.14.13.72 is a transferred/obsolete entry, now reclassified as EC 1.14.18.9 (4alpha-methylsterol monooxygenase, ergosterol/sterol C4-demethylation pathway); no fusion with another catalytic activity is described.
1.14.13.72.evidence: ExPASy ENZYME entry confirms transfer to EC 1.14.18.9; no bifunctional/multifunctional literature found

1.2.1.3.rationale: Generic NAD+-dependent (non-acetylating) aldehyde dehydrogenase; distinct from AdhE's acetylating activity (EC 1.2.1.10). No literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.1.rationale: Alcohol dehydrogenase is overwhelmingly characterized as a standalone, monofunctional enzyme across eukaryotes and most bacteria. A well-known exception, bacterial/protozoal AdhE, fuses this activity with acetylating acetaldehyde dehydrogenase (EC 1.2.1.10) on one polypeptide, but this is a specific anaerobic-fermentation variant rather than the characteristic form of EC 1.1.1.1.
1.1.1.1.evidence: PMID 38875756 (bifunctional AdhE in Cryptosporidium, cited as a known exception, not the default form); ExPASy EC 1.1.1.1 cross-references several ADHE_* UniProt entries

1.3.3.6.rationale: Acyl-CoA oxidase (peroxisomal beta-oxidation entry enzyme, e.g. ACOX1/ACOX2); no evidence of a second fused catalytic activity.

1.1.1.35.rationale: 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity is one of three fused catalytic domains -- enoyl-CoA hydratase (EC 4.2.1.17), Delta3,Delta2-enoyl-CoA isomerase (EC 5.3.3.8), and this dehydrogenase -- on the single-polypeptide peroxisomal enzyme EHHADH (UniProt Q08426), which UniProt itself describes as a 'peroxisomal trifunctional enzyme'. This is distinct from the monofunctional long-chain-specific dehydrogenase (EC 1.1.1.211).
1.1.1.35.evidence: UniProt Q08426 (EHHADH/PBE/MFE1); ExPASy EC 1.1.1.35 notes 'broad specificity to acyl chain-length (cf. EC 1.1.1.211)'

2.4.1.17.rationale: UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT superfamily); broad substrate promiscuity is well documented but no literature describes a second fused catalytic activity.

6.2.1.3.rationale: Butanoate-CoA ligase (medium/long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase); no literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.21.rationale: Aldose reductase/alditol:NAD+ oxidoreductase (aldo-keto reductase family); no literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.145.rationale: 3beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase/Delta5-Delta4-isomerase (3beta-HSD, e.g. HSD3B1/HSD3B2) is a single polypeptide experimentally shown to carry out both the NAD+-dependent 3beta-dehydrogenase reaction and the steroid double-bond isomerase reaction sequentially on one active site/enzyme.
1.1.1.145.evidence: PMID 7673125 (NADH-induced conformational change mediating sequential 3beta-HSD/isomerase activities); PMID 10514560

4.2.1.17.rationale: Enoyl-CoA hydratase activity is one of three catalytic domains (hydratase + Delta3,Delta2-enoyl-CoA isomerase EC 5.3.3.8 + 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase EC 1.1.1.35) fused on the single-polypeptide peroxisomal enzyme EHHADH; it is also the HADHA (alpha-subunit) activity of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein complex, paired with the HADHB thiolase subunit.
4.2.1.17.evidence: UniProt Q08426 (EHHADH); PMID 41500837, 39088276, 40790338 (mitochondrial trifunctional protein / HADHA)

2.3.1.16.rationale: This 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase activity is carried by HADHB, the beta-subunit of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein (a stable hetero-octameric complex) whose alpha-subunit (HADHA) additionally carries enoyl-CoA hydratase and long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activities, giving the complex three fused catalytic activities. A free-standing monofunctional form (e.g. peroxisomal ACAA1) also exists under this same EC, hence medium confidence.
2.3.1.16.evidence: PMID 41500837, 39088276, 40790338 (mitochondrial trifunctional protein deficiency, HADHB); ExPASy EC 2.3.1.16 cross-references ECHB_* (HADHB) UniProt entries

5.3.3.1.rationale: Steroid Delta-isomerase activity in this reaction context is the second catalytic activity of the single-polypeptide 3beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase/Delta5-Delta4-isomerase enzyme (3beta-HSD), which also carries the EC 1.1.1.145 dehydrogenase activity.
5.3.3.1.evidence: PMID 7673125 (sequential 3beta-HSD/isomerase activities on one enzyme); PMID 10514560

2.7.8.29.rationale: L-serine-phosphatidylethanolamine phosphatidyltransferase (phosphatidylserine synthase); no literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.

4.1.1.65.rationale: Phosphatidylserine decarboxylase (PISD); no literature found describing a fused second catalytic activity.
